slides.texte_overlay:
how you stand out in your
20s
Build something outside your job. A side project, a sports team, a small business. Making something of your own sets you apart from most people your age.
Take your health seriously early. Train, sleep and eat well while others ignore it. In ten years the difference will be huge.
Learn to ask for feedback. "What could I do better?" Most people avoid criticism. Seeking it makes you grow twice as fast.
Show up early and prepared. To meetings, interviews, dates. Being reliable and ready is surprisingly rare in your 20s. Little by little, it adds up.
Read more than you scroll. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it gives me ideas and stories most people simply don't have.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It gives me ideas and stories most people simply don't have.

slides.texte_overlay: Build real friendships with older people. Mentors, bosses, family friends. Their experience can save you years of mistakes.
Be kind when it's not expected. In a competitive world, generosity stands out more than any achievement on your CV. Kindness is remembered long after titles are forgotten.
